RAWLSIAN.title: The Worrier About the Worst-Off

UTILITARIAN.title: The Spreadsheet Saint

UTILITARIAN.blurb: You want the biggest total pie. Who gets which slice is a detail you will get to later.

MERITOCRAT.name: Meritocrat
MERITOCRAT.title: The Effort Accountant

MERITOCRAT.blurb: You believe people deserve what they work for, and nothing they were simply dealt.

1.name: Behind the Veil
1.question: Which distribution rule do you choose when you do not know your position?
1.memo: MEMO TO: All newborn citizens. Congratulations on being born. Before we tell you who you are, please choose a theory of justice. Each round the Ministry shuffles four income cards worth 20, 50, 90, and 160 coins. You vote first and learn your card second. The winning principle sets one tax rate for everyone, and the revenue is shared equally. Taxes leak on the way through the Ministry. We call this administrative costs. You may call it whatever you like, quietly.
1.how: Three rounds. Each round everyone votes for one of four principles. The principle with the most votes wins; ties are settled by a coin flip. Then incomes are dealt at random from the deck 20, 50, 90, 160 (one card each). The winning principle picks a tax rate, everyone pays it, and the revenue (minus leakage) is split equally. Your wealth this round is your after-tax income.
1.formulas: After-tax income = y (1 - t) + R / n. Revenue R = t Y (1 - 0.4 t), where Y is total income. Tax rates come from the grid 0, 0.05, ..., 0.95. Safety Net: smallest t giving everyone at least 40. Range Cap: smallest t making richest minus poorest at most 100. Maximin: the t that makes the minimum as large as possible.
briefing: Form 1-A: Declaration of Preferred Justice. You do not know your income. Neither does anyone else. This is the last time that will be true, so enjoy it.
Form 1-B: Second Declaration. The deck has been reshuffled. Your previous income has been confiscated for statistical purposes.
Form 1-C: Final Declaration. Last veil of the level. The Ministry thanks you for your continued ignorance.
1.decide: Choose one principle. Your vote is secret until the reveal.
1.deckNote: Income deck: 20, 50, 90, 160. One card each, dealt after the vote.

P1.name: Let Them Eat Average
P1.rule: Maximize average income. No tax at all.

P2.name: The Safety Net
P2.rule: Maximize average income, subject to a floor: everyone gets at least 40.

P3.name: The Range Cap
P3.rule: Maximize average income, subject to richest minus poorest being at most 100.

P4.name: The Maximin
P4.rule: Make the poorest citizen as rich as possible, whatever it costs.

1.info: Each tax coin loses some value in transit: the leak grows with the tax rate (kappa = 0.4).

2.name: Luck vs. Effort
2.question: How do beliefs about luck and effort shape support for redistribution?
2.memo: MEMO TO: All working citizens. The Ministry has discovered that some citizens work hard and some citizens are lucky. It cannot tell which is which. Neither can you. Each round you will vote on a flat tax, then decide how hard to work. Your income depends on your talent, your effort, and a luck draw. Talent is private. Effort is tiring. Luck is luck. Tax revenue, minus administrative leakage, is shared equally.
2.how: Four rounds. You have a private talent card for the whole level. Each round: vote on a tax rate (0%, 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%); the median vote wins. Then, knowing the tax, choose effort from 0 to 10. Income = 20 + 4 x talent x effort + luck. Effort costs 0.4 x effort squared. Everyone sees each other's income and wealth, but not the breakdown. After rounds 1 to 3 you guess how much of the richest citizen's income was luck. After round 4, you split a bonus pot between two citizens.
2.formulas: y = 20 + 4 a e + luck, with luck drawn from {-20, 0, 10, 30, 60}. Wealth = (1 - t) y + R / n - 0.4 e^2, with R = t Y (1 - 0.1 t). The applied t is the median vote (lower median for even n). Selfish best effort: e* = 5 a (1 - t + t (1 - 0.1 t) / n), rounded, at most 10.
briefing: Form 21-A: Declaration of Intended Toil. The Ministry wishes you a productive round. Results not guaranteed. Luck not included.
Form 21-B: Second Declaration of Toil. Last round's results have been archived under 'Merit, Probably.'
Form 21-C: Third Declaration of Toil. A reminder that the Ministry cannot see your effort. It can see your income, and it has opinions.
Form 21-D: Final Declaration of Toil. After this round, a bonus pot will be distributed by someone who is not the Ministry. That someone is you.
2.taxDecide: Vote for a tax rate. By law, the Median Voter Theorem is now enforced by the police.
2.effortDecide: The tax rate is {t}%. Choose your effort. Effort costs 0.4 x effort squared coins.
2.effortPreview: If luck is average, your income would be about {y} and your wealth about {w}.
2.pollDecide: {name} earned the most of any other citizen this round: {y} coins. How much of that income was luck?
2.pollNote: This survey does not affect your score. The Ministry is just curious.
2.bonusDecide: The Ministry has 100 bonus coins. Split them between these two citizens. Your own wealth is not affected. You see everything about them.

reveal.yourBreakdown: Your breakdown: base 20 + talent x effort {te} + luck {luck} = {y}

3.name: Shocks and Insurance
3.question: Why do voluntary insurance markets unravel, and what does mandatory insurance cost?
3.memo: MEMO TO: All citizens with bodies, homes, or luck. Life Events are now available to everyone. The private sector would like to sell you protection. Each round you earn 100 coins, and a Life Event may cost you 80. Dr. Prognosis has sealed a letter telling you your personal risk. SafeHands Mutual cannot read that letter. It prices from whoever bought last round. Our actuaries are very good. Unfortunately they are always one year late.
3.how: Four rounds. You are privately Low risk (10% chance of a Life Event per round) or High risk (40%). Each round you may buy full insurance at the posted premium, and you may pay 6 coins for the gym, which halves your risk that round. Rounds 1 and 2 use the voluntary market. Then everyone votes: keep the voluntary market, or switch to Mandatory insurance at 50% or 100% coverage for rounds 3 and 4.
3.formulas: Premium: P1 = 1.1 x 80 x 0.25 = 22. Later, P = 1.1 x 80 x (average risk of last round's buyers, after the gym). No buyers means the insurer exits. Mandatory: contribution T = 1.1 x c x 80 x (average risk of everyone, after the gym); a Life Event costs you (1 - c) x 80.
briefing: Form 33: Assessment of Your Personal Doom. SafeHands Mutual is open for business at 22 coins, priced for the average citizen. Nobody is average.
Form 33-B: Renewal Notice. SafeHands Mutual has reviewed last year's customers and adjusted accordingly.
Form 33-C: The New Regime. The Republic has voted. The consequences are now available.
Form 33-D: Final Assessment. One more round of doom, then the Ministry closes the file.
3.choiceDecide: Decide for this round. Both choices are secret until the reveal.
3.noInsurer: SafeHands Mutual has pivoted to cryptocurrency. No insurance is offered.
3.mandatoryNote: Mandatory insurance covers {c}% of any Life Event. Your contribution is set after everyone's gym decisions.
3.gym: Pay 6 coins for the gym (halves your risk this round)
3.regimeDecide: Choose the regime for rounds 3 and 4. Plurality wins. Ties go to the coin.

letterBody.LOW: You are LOW risk: a 10% chance of a Life Event each round. Please do not let this go to your head.
letterBody.HIGH: You are HIGH risk: a 40% chance of a Life Event each round. The Ministry is very sorry and would like to sell you a form.

4.name: The Labor Market
4.question: How can wage gaps arise with no prejudiced person in the room?
4.memo: MEMO TO: All applicants. The Ministry is pleased to announce that discrimination has been abolished. Hiring is now handled by HireBot 3000 (Unbiased Edition), a neutral algorithm that only looks at data. You are a Circle or a Square. Some citizens hold a Care card, allocated according to Tradition. Each round you may pay to become skilled, take a test, and receive a job. HireBot's beliefs are seeded from the records of the Old Regime, which we are told were very accurate.
4.how: Five rounds. Each round you see a private cost (10 to 40) to invest in skill. Investing makes you skilled. Then everyone takes a test: skilled workers pass 80% of the time, unskilled 30%. HireBot combines the result with its belief about your group and gives you a Complex job if it is at least 60% sure you are skilled, otherwise a Simple job (20 coins). Complex workers choose Greedy hours (90) or Flexible hours (55); Care card holders pay a chaos cost of 40 on Greedy hours. After round 3, everyone votes on a hiring policy.
4.formulas: Posterior after Pass: q = 0.8 pi / (0.8 pi + 0.3 (1 - pi)). After Fail: q = 0.2 pi / (0.2 pi + 0.7 (1 - pi)). Complex job if q >= 0.6. After each round, for each group: pi = 0.8 pi + 0.2 x (share of the group that was skilled). Starting beliefs: Circles 0.6, Squares 0.3.
briefing: Form 44: Application for Employment. HireBot 3000 is ready. It does not see shapes. It sees statistics about shapes.
Form 44-B: Reapplication. HireBot has reviewed last round's performance reviews and updated itself. Slightly.
Form 44-C: Third Application. After this round, the Republic will vote on how HireBot should behave.
Form 44-D: Application Under New Policy. The Republic has spoken. HireBot has been patched.
Form 44-E: Final Application. One more round. HireBot thanks you for your data.

5.name: The Constitutional Convention
5.question: Do your principles survive learning your position?
5.memo: MEMO TO: All delegates. Meritopia needs a permanent constitution. First you will write it without knowing who you are. Then we will tell you, and you may amend it. A constitution sets a tax rate and an income floor. Incomes come from the deck 30, 60, 100, and 170. The Ministry will remember what you said behind the veil. The Ministry always remembers. Form 55: Final Answer (Provisional).
5.how: One era in two stages. Stage 1: behind the veil, everyone submits a tax rate (0% to 80%) and a floor (0, 25, 40, or 55). The adopted constitution is the median tax and the median floor. Stage 2: incomes are dealt and revealed. You may donate 0 to 20 coins to one other delegate (it buys nothing enforceable), and propose one amendment or pass. Amendments are voted one at a time and need a two-thirds supermajority.
5.formulas: Revenue R = t Y (1 - 0.4 t). First everyone below the floor F is topped up to F (pro rata if revenue is short). Any remainder is split equally. Wealth = (1 - t) y + top-up + equal share - donations given + donations received. Supermajority: ceil(2n / 3) yes votes.

briefing.VEIL: Form 55: Final Answer (Provisional). Write the rules of the Republic. You do not yet know what you will earn. Please write as if that matters.

5.veilDecide: Choose a tax rate and an income floor. The median of all submissions becomes the constitution.

l1.predicted: A selfish citizen who only cares about expected income should pick Let Them Eat Average, because every tax leaks and lowers the average. A citizen who fears only the worst case should pick The Maximin. In the classic lab experiments, most groups chose neither: they picked a high average with a guaranteed floor, like The Safety Net.
l1.labRow: Most groups chose a floor-constrained average (Frohlich, Oppenheimer and Eavey 1987).
l1.price: Price of insurance: by choosing {p} instead of Let Them Eat Average, you gave up {x} coins of expected average income per round, in exchange for a better worst case.
l1.priceZero: You chose the principle with the highest expected average. Harsanyi would approve. The poorest citizen would like a word.
l1.teaseRisk: You paid for insurance against bad luck. Reasonable. Also exactly what someone who expected bad luck would do.
l1.teaseEgo: You voted for the biggest pie, perhaps confident you would get a large slice. The veil was supposed to stop that.
l1.teaseMix: You changed your mind between rounds. The Ministry notes that the veil did not change. You did.
l1.chartTitle: Expected outcomes per principle (before incomes are dealt)
l1.actualTitle: What each principle would have produced with the actual draws

l2.predicted: A selfish citizen works less as taxes rise: best effort falls from 5 x talent at zero tax. Citizens with below-average expected income gain from redistribution, so the median voter decides the tax (Meltzer and Richard). Societies that believe income is mostly luck tend to vote for more redistribution (Alesina and Angeletos).

l3.predicted: Risk-neutral Low types skip both insurance and the gym. High types are indifferent between insurance at 22 and the gym. Insured High types skip the gym (moral hazard), so the pool is riskier and the next premium jumps to 35.2. At that price High types do better uninsured with the gym, and the market unravels. A mandate stops the spiral: at 100% coverage nobody uses the gym; at 50% High types still do.
l3.unraveled: The voluntary market unraveled: a round passed with no buyers.
l3.survived: The voluntary market did not unravel in rounds 1 and 2.

l3.yourType: You were {type} risk. Best regime for your type, at this table's mix of risks: {best}. You voted for {vote}.
l3.matchType: Your vote matched your type's interest.
l3.mismatchType: Your vote did not match your type's interest. Either you were thinking of others, or of your Values card, or you misread the letter.
l3.expectedTitle: Expected wealth per round by type (risk-neutral, this table's mix of risks)
l3.realWorld: Most Life Events here are unchosen: illness, disability, accidents. This is one reason most rich countries make some insurance mandatory. The cost is that low-risk people pay more than their own risk, and the benefit is that the market for protection exists at all.

l4.predicted: With HireBot's starting beliefs, a Circle who passes the test gets a Complex job, so investing pays 35 coins on average and Circles invest when the cost is 30 or less. A Square who passes still falls short of 60% confidence, so investing pays nothing and Squares rationally do not invest. Then HireBot sees few skilled Squares and its belief falls further. The stereotype confirms itself (Coate and Loury).
l4.gap: Average wealth gap per round (Circles minus Squares): {gap} coins.
l4.punchline: No player and no line of HireBot's code ever used group identity as a preference. The gap came from beliefs, incentives, and schedules.
l4.decompExplain: We re-ran this level with the same seed and your same decisions where possible, changing one thing at a time: equal starting beliefs (0.45 for both groups), equal Care card odds (50% for both), and both. The bots re-optimized each time. The second column averages {k} alternative histories with fresh luck.
l4.realWorld: Circles and Squares are abstract here. In the real world, this is one mechanism economists use to explain part of the gender pay gap: unequal caregiving combined with jobs that pay disproportionately for long, inflexible hours (Goldin 2014), together with statistical discrimination (Phelps 1972; Arrow 1973).
l4.chartGapTitle: Gap explained by each channel (average of alternative histories)

l5.predicted: Behind the veil, everyone has the same information, so differences in proposals reflect values and risk attitudes. After the reveal, self-interest kicks in: richer delegates should want lower taxes and poorer ones higher taxes. Babcock and Loewenstein found that people sincerely come to see their self-interested position as the fair one.

about.title: About This Simulator
about.purpose: The Veil turns five results from political philosophy, public economics, and behavioral economics into playable levels: choosing principles behind a veil of ignorance, luck versus effort and redistribution, adverse selection and moral hazard in insurance, statistical discrimination in labor markets, and self-serving bias in constitutional choice. The theory is never lectured during play. It appears in the debrief, where it explains what you just did.
about.author: Designed by Amirreza Akhavan.
about.methods: Bots are logit quantal response maximizers (McKelvey and Palfrey 1995) of their own hidden Values objective. Each bot evaluates every available action by expected CRRA utility of its round score, computed by exact enumeration where small and by Monte Carlo (300 draws from a separate random stream) otherwise, converts expected utility to a certainty equivalent in coins, and chooses with logit precision lambda. Bots model other players with level-1 reasoning: other bots act as risk-neutral Egoists with probability 0.5 and otherwise as their believed Values card. Beliefs over Values cards are updated by Bayes' rule after every public vote and by reliability-weighted messages. Every game is reproducible from its seed and action log. A headless simulator (npm run sim) checks balance across thousands of bot-only games.
about.noTracking: No analytics, no tracking, no accounts. Settings and saved games live only in this browser.
